solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mental attitude, note, during inconclusive time at court

indicators.note: during says the note sits within the period of play that follows

parts.note: halfway through a tennis set, play on court has not yet reached a conclusion: mid-set

explanation.surface: A tennis player's psychology is tested partway through an undecided set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At court' means a tennis court, not a law court: the moment halfway through a set is MID-SET, with N put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed way of thinking or habitual outlook is a person's mental attitude.

clue.text: Endless insolence contributing to staff hostility

indicators.note: contributing to says the shortened insolence goes into the staff

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff

indicators.note: Endless says the last letter of the insolence word goes

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, insolence

explanation.surface: Constant rudeness among employees breeds ill feeling in the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a ceremonial stick; 'Endless' trims the insolence word before 'contributing to' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will and the desire to harm, a form of hostility.

clue.text: A lot of moonshine filling most of neighbouring astronomical object

indicators.note: filling says the shortened nonsense goes inside the other shortened word
most of says the final letter of the word for neighbouring is dropped

parts.note: near means neighbouring

indicators.note: A lot of says most but not all of the word for moonshine is used

parts.note: moonshine means nonsense, which is bull

explanation.surface: A lot of moonlight spills over a nearby celestial body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonshine' is nonsense, not moonlight or liquor: BUL goes inside NEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space, one kind of astronomical object.

clue.text: Ecological concept worse with polar melting?

indicators.note: melting says these words lose their shape and re-form in a different order

explanation.surface: An environmental idea is made worse by melting polar ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melting' rearranges WORSE and POLAR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy taken from sunlight is a renewable, green idea central to ecological thinking.

clue.text: One apprehended by the force?

indicators.note: apprehended by says the one is caught inside the other letters

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The force' looks like the police but is THE plus F, holding I; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber is the classic example of a person the police arrest.

clue.text: Painful disease mostly a scourge? One would see the cards dealt differently

definitions.text: One would see the cards dealt differently

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the disease is dropped

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints, especially the big toe
a lash is a whip, a scourge

explanation.surface: Someone suffers from a painful disease that is almost as bad as being whipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is better known as a Hungarian stew; Chambers also gives it as a bridge term, which the definition uses.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a goulash is a redeal in which the unshuffled cards are handed out in batches, so the hands fall very differently.

clue.text: Rig water tanks after finally identifying source of cracks?

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow that single letter
finally says only the last letter of identifying is taken
tanks, as slang for collapses or wrecks, says the letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A plumber is told to fit water tanks once the cause of the leaks is found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracks' are wisecracks, not leaks; 'tanks' is a verb rearranging RIG WATER into AGWRITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes jokes for comedians produces wisecracks, so is their source.

clue.text: Goes heading off in vessels

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: goes, as in 'takes a turn', gives turns

explanation.surface: Someone sets off in boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' is the noun plural, as in 'have a go': turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, so they are vessels.

clue.text: A sport — I'll occupy half of game in defence

parts.note: polo is a sport played on horseback

indicators.note: occupy says the I takes up a place within the half word
half of says only the first two letters of game are taken

parts.note: I'll is 'I will', so the I is what does the occupying

explanation.surface: A sportsman vows to play part of a game in a defensive position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll occupy' reads as 'I will occupy': the I alone is the piece, and 'half of' takes the first two letters of 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's beliefs or conduct.

clue.text: Political meeting shows expressions of affection about rising idiots

indicators.note: about says the embraces go round the other part

parts.note: hugs are embraces, expressions of affection

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the idiots are read from the bottom up

parts.note: nits is a British word for idiots (nitwits)

explanation.surface: A rally shows affection for idiots who are getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hustings are election meetings where candidates address voters, so a political meeting.

clue.text: Calumny I ignored, retaining a name

indicators.note: retaining says the shortened word holds the a inside it
ignored says the I is left out of the calumny

parts.note: libel is a written calumny, a damaging false statement

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a slander while keeping their good name.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from LIBEL to leave LBEL, then put A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag or designation is a name, as when we pin a description on someone or something.

clue.text: Using one source of intelligence possibly seen as this?

definitions.text: Using one source of intelligence possibly seen as this?

indicators.note: source of says only the first letter of intelligence is taken
possibly says the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Exploiting a single informant might be thought a clever move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges USING, ONE and I (the start of 'intelligence'); the whole clue then describes the answer, since a clever use of one source is itself clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Making much of a single source of information would be considered clever and inventive.

clue.text: Volatile liquid from Switzerland left room for being refined

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

indicators.note: being refined says these letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A volatile liquid from a Swiss lab left space for further refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being refined' is the anagram signal, not chemistry; CH is the vehicle code for Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweet-smelling anaesthetic evaporates readily, so it is a volatile liquid.

clue.text: Contributor to downfall of industry spurning technology

indicators.note: Contributor to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something played a part in the decline of manufacturing that rejected modern machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lo-fi sound or style deliberately rejects polished, high-tech production values.

clue.text: No great choice of clothing for daredevil sportsman

definitions.meaning: read as base (low, poor) plus jumper (sweater): a cheap sweater is a poor choice
someone who parachutes from buildings, antennas, spans or cliffs

explanation.surface: A cheap sweater is a bad pick for a thrill-seeking athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is the British word for a sweater; 'base' means low or inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme sport of leaping from fixed structures with a parachute is practised by daredevils.

clue.text: Hard to resign unexpectedly, protracted negotiations ensuing

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters of these words come out in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: An official finds it hard to step down suddenly while long talks are continuing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' shuffles all of HARD TO RESIGN; 'ensuing' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, lengthy bargaining, like dealers haggling at a horse fair, is protracted negotiation.

clue.text: Quantity of fish and quantity of game — youngster may find it a burden

definitions.text: youngster may find it a burden

parts.note: a school is a large group of fish swimming together
a bag is the amount of game shot by a hunter

explanation.surface: A fisherman's catch and a hunter's haul are a heavy load for a child to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A child carries books to lessons in a satchel, which can be heavy and a burden.

clue.text: I stop, mostly to consume cooked bun in historic city

indicators.note: to consume says the shortened word swallows the reworked bun
mostly says the last letter of the stopping word is dropped

parts.note: to stall is to stop

indicators.note: cooked says the letters of bun are worked into another order

explanation.surface: A traveller pauses mainly to eat a baked bun in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: STALL loses its last letter to give STAL, which takes in NBU (BUN rearranged, from 'cooked').
explanation.definitionFit: The former Constantinople and Byzantium is a city with a long, famous history.

clue.text: Skilful fiction, observed to dismiss love

parts.note: a tale is a story, a work of fiction

indicators.note: to dismiss says the love is sent out of the other word

parts.note: noted means observed
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A clever story was seen to send love packing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gifted with natural ability is skilful.

clue.text: Wind damage in church — Rector's first man controlling source of hiss?

parts.note: to wind is to snake, twisting along

indicators.note: in says the damage sits inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to harm is to damage

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of Rector is taken

explanation.surface: Storm damage to a church; the rector is the first to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is the verb (rhymes with 'find'), not a gale. The definition's 'source of hiss' is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who makes a cobra rise and sway to a pipe is controlling a hissing creature.

clue.text: Historic coin, an affair mostly containing gold

indicators.note: containing says the shortened affair holds the gold
mostly says the last letter of the affair is dropped

parts.note: a fling is a brief affair
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An old coin is mostly an affair with gold inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The FLORIN was a British two-shilling coin before decimal currency.
explanation.definitionFit: This former British two-shilling piece is a coin of the past.

clue.text: A poor place to accommodate unknown refugee's aim

indicators.note: to accommodate says the poor place houses the unknown

parts.note: a slum is a squalid, poor district
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A deprived area houses a stranger who is seeking shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fleeing persecution seeks protection and sanctuary in another country.

clue.text: Peak interpretation of the missing link?

parts.note: the ape is the link in the chain of descent from which man evolved
X is the mark used to show something is missing or wrong

explanation.surface: A summit offers a reading of the evolutionary gap between apes and humans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interpretation of the missing link' asks for a fresh reading of the phrase: X (missing) and APE (link), written APE then X.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or tip, so it is a peak.

clue.text: Removal of creatures from harbour is a defensive measure

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a cull is the selective killing of animals to reduce numbers

explanation.surface: Clearing animals out of a harbour is described as a protective step.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's grille gate, dropped to block the entrance, is a defensive measure.

clue.text: Scientific innovator turning up in medical setting

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pioneering scientist arrives in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the letters from the bottom; 'in' also signals that they sit within 'medical setting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla pioneered alternating-current electrical systems, so he was an inventor.

clue.text: Viral infection billions contracted in error

parts.note: flu is influenza, a viral infection
B is the short form of billions

explanation.surface: A virus catches billions of people by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' looks like catching an illness but means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A flub is a blunder or a botched attempt, so a mistake.

clue.text: Speed and bustle energised part of politician's campaign

parts.note: bat is speed, as in 'going at a fair bat'

indicators.note: energised says the word's letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Fast pace and lively activity give a politician's campaign its energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energised' is the anagram signal; 'bat' for pace is British informal usage, as in 'at a fair bat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach carrying a party leader round the country during an election is a feature of campaigning.

clue.text: Danger from each disease unending

parts.note: per means each, as in 'a pound per head'

indicators.note: unending says the last letter of the word for disease is lost

parts.note: ill is a disease or ailment

explanation.surface: Each disease that goes on and on poses a threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious risk, a synonym of danger.

clue.text: Boy and man recoiling, jabbed by black insect

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: jabbed by says another letter is stuck into the reversed man
recoiling says the word for man springs back, read from right to left

parts.note: guy is a man
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A boy and a man flinch as they are stabbed by something black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recoiling' reverses only the man, and 'jabbed by' sticks the black letter into that reversed word; 'Boy' stays as written in front.
explanation.definitionFit: This red, black-spotted beetle (US name for the ladybird) is a type of insect.

clue.text: Current memory involves US city laser, perhaps

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: involves says the memory takes in the city

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Electrical current and computer memory are both needed for a laser in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Laser is formed from the initials of 'light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation', so it is an example of such a word.
